page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v5 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing hyperthreading. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware includes 161 GB of bundled local SSD storage for ephemeral operations, and the instance operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent mid-tier single-threaded compute performance, supported by instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance achieved an average Geekbench single-core score of 1654.0 and demonstrated standard throughput in static web serving at 6.51 GB/sec. In contrast, multi-threaded throughput and memory subsystems benchmark in lower percentiles. The Geekbench multi-core score of 3522.0, PassMark CPU score of 5931.19, and large-block memory read bandwidth of 30.07 GB/sec reflect the limits of a 2-core physical topology and constrained memory bandwidth.

The 1:2 memory ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency for compute-focused tasks that do not require large RAM allocations, avoiding expenditure on unused memory capacity. However, the 8.0 GB total capacity and lower multi-threaded throughput limit suitability for heavy in-memory data processing or highly parallel compute. The D4lds_v5 is practical for containerized microservices, CI/CD compilation tasks, static web front-ends, batch computing, and utility workloads leveraging local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v5 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores clocked at 2.8 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM and 161 GB of local SSD storage. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation, it reduces resource overhead for tasks that prioritize compute cycles over memory capacity. Synthetic testing demonstrates standard single-threaded CPU capability, reaching a single-core Geekbench score of 1654.0 and static web serving throughput of 6.51 GB/sec. However, multi-core throughput and memory subsystem benchmarks place in the lower quartile, restricting its utility for highly concurrent or memory-intensive operations. The instance lacks discrete GPU acceleration. The hardware configuration functions effectively for lightweight web serving, CI/CD compilation tasks, containerized microservices, and general compute workloads requiring fast, localized temporary disk storage without large memory footprints.
